SUMMARY: hairstyle a chin-length waved bob with a side-swept fringe; costume a heavy leather work apron with rolled sleeves, a tool harness and one big gauntlet glove — a hands-on engineer's shape; design idea Nested charcoal-black apron panels fold across one another like a compact reactor pile, their honey-lit piping ending at a solid frost-white terminal flap.; face a cool, aloof beauty; expression resolute.

A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Fermium (페르뮴) itself — the sovereign of the Fermium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a youthful face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; fair skin; heart-shaped face; rounder almond eyes of natural size; azure-blue eyes; gently arched, slender brows; a nose with a gentle aquiline curve; slender lips of natural width.
Body and hair: toned athletic-curvy, full-busted with rounded hips build; a chin-length waved bob with a side-swept fringe; glossy graphite-black hair with a warm ember-red glow banked deep inside, like coals kept alive overnight.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a firm, resolute look with calm, steady eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: fermium: element 100, the first to reach three digits, found together with her twin einsteinium in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test in 1952, and named for the physicist who lit the first nuclear reactor, a pile of graphite blocks stacked in a squash court beneath the stands of a university sports field in the winter of 1942; she is the end of the road for building heavier elements by feeding neutrons to a reactor, because the next step splits apart almost at once, a wall no neutron can climb; her longest-lived form lasts only about a hundred days, and no one has ever gathered enough of her to see.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a heavy leather work apron with rolled sleeves, a tool harness and one big gauntlet glove — a hands-on engineer's shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Design idea: Nested charcoal-black apron panels fold across one another like a compact reactor pile, their honey-lit piping ending at a solid frost-white terminal flap.
Colours: banked-coal graphite black, warm ember red, hearth-glow honey, frost white.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1912, a vast stoking hall beneath the stands of a university sports field in winter: a great round pile built from layer upon layer of black graphite blocks, slanting shadows of wooden bleachers overhead, frosty winter sunlight through high windows and snow drifted against the glass.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Fm) and atomic number (100) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
